  "reason": "The student's claim contains two major factual errors. First, dropout does not 'increase every activation at inference'; rather, it is disabled during inference (or uses a scaling factor like 1/p) to prevent the network from relying on specific dropped units, effectively making activations deterministic and consistent. Second, dropout actively disables activations (by setting them to zero) during training to prevent overfitting. The claim contradicts the fundamental definition of dropout as a regularization technique used during training that is turned off at inference.",
